title: Auth — Step-up Approve Request
description: A relying party asks an approver (typically a wallet or a VTA) to ratify an AAL elevation for a subject's session, or — bound to one operation — to approve that one act without elevating any session, and states which kinds of evidence it will accept, including a statement by one of the subject's bound step-up approvers.

subject.description: The VID whose session is being elevated, or — for a step-up bound to one operation — the VID whose act that operation is. The approver MUST verify this is a VID it can speak for.

sessionId.description: The session the relying party wants elevated. Opaque to the approver. Absent only when the step-up is bound to one operation that arrived without a session (a signed Trust Task document, for instance); see `boundTo`.

boundTo.description: Present when the step-up authorizes exactly one operation rather than raising a session's assurance level. An opaque relying-party identifier for that operation — for an operation that arrived as a signed document, a digest of its type and payload salted with `challenge`. Copied into a step-up approver's statement, and echoed by a `recorded` approve-response acknowledgement. Not a capability: the binding is the relying party's own state.

challenge.description: base64url-encoded nonce the approver will include in the approve-response signature, the WebAuthn assertion, or the step-up approver's statement. ≥128 bits entropy.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation of WHY the relying party is asking (e.g. "confirm transfer of 1000 USD to bob.example"). Surfaced to the user by the approver for consent. SHOULD be specific enough that a user can refuse intelligently.

targetAcr.description: The acr the relying party expects on the elevated session. Approvers MAY refuse if they cannot deliver this level.

accepts.description: Every approve-response evidence kind the relying party will accept for this step-up, and no other (see auth/step-up/approve-response/0.6 `evidence`). Replaces 0.3's optional `acceptableEvidence`. An approver that can satisfy none of them SHOULD refuse with `methodUnsupported`.

webauthn.description: WebAuthn `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions` the approver passes to the platform passkey API when producing `webauthn` evidence. Present exactly when `accepts` lists `webauthn`. Its `challenge` MUST equal `payload.challenge` so the resulting assertion binds the same nonce the relying party bound server-side.

approvers.description: The step-up approvers bound to `subject` that the relying party will accept a statement from (auth/step-up/approver/attest/0.1, purpose `stepUp`). Present exactly when `accepts` lists `approverSigned`. Names factors, not authorities: an approver confers nothing, and the relying party re-checks the binding when the statement arrives.

ttl.description: Seconds within which the relying party expects the approve-response. Approvers SHOULD treat as advisory — the relying party's own expiry policy is authoritative.

Response.title: Auth Step-up Approve Request — response payload
Response.description: Synchronous ack from the approver acknowledging it received the request and will (or will not) deliver an approve-response. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/auth/step-up/approve-request/0.4#response.

status.description: `accepted` means the approver received the request and will return an approve-response (typically via DIDComm). `refused` means it will not — `reason` MUST be set.
